facts.text: RetroEnv is a gymnasium.Env subclass that provides a Gym interface to classic video games
The environment metadata declares the render modes human and rgb_array and 60.0 video frames per second
The constructor defaults to Actions.FILTERED restricted actions, one player, Observations.IMAGE and render_mode human
The buttons of a game come from the emulator core metadata and their count is num_buttons
With the default restricted-actions mode the action space is MultiBinary(num_buttons * players)
The observation space is Box(low=0, high=255) with the shape of the screen or RAM buffer and dtype uint8
The observation is an RGB image from the emulator screen by default; obs_type RAM returns the RAM buffer instead
The default observations are RGB images of the game, and RAM values can be viewed instead
step advances one emulator frame and returns (observation, reward, bool(done), False, dict(info))
reset accepts seed and options and seeds gymnasium's RNG with super().reset(seed=seed); it restores the initial state, presses no buttons, advances the emulator once and returns (observation, {})
Reward and done come from the game data (current_reward and is_done) and info is lookup_all
The screen is cropped to the game's crop_info rectangle and optionally rotation-corrected
close deletes the emulator and closes the viewer
stable_retro.make() checks the ROM file path and returns RetroEnv(game, state, inttype=inttype, **kwargs)
The README says ROMs are not included and must be obtained and imported, and names one non-commercial Airstriker Genesis ROM included for testing
The emulators are deterministic, so playback of a recorded button sequence gives the same output each time

determinism.notes: reset(seed) seeds gymnasium's RNG (retro_env.py:261) while the emulator state comes from the game's savestate (retro_env.py:263-267), and the emulators are deterministic for the same actions (docs/python.md:51); the fake mirrors a fixed game state and is deterministic too

gaps: no emulator core, game data or ROM handling is modelled: the fake backend is pure Python and its rewards, termination and info are test data, not a game's scenario rules (retro_env.py:366-373)
the fake returns a flat 60-element uint8 stand-in for an RGB frame; the real screen shape depends on the emulator core and the game's crop_info (retro_env.py:157-161, 333-351)
no rendering is modelled: render() is not implemented by the fake; only observations are served
the seed seeds gymnasium's RNG, not the emulator (retro_env.py:261-267); the fake mirrors a fixed state and does not draw a random start state
snapshot and restore are not offered: RetroEnv exposes no get_state/set_state, so the bridge reports snapshot_restore false
the fake was never compared with the upstream emulator; the upstream environment was not run here

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: the runtime latch refuses step and reset after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears it, and the fake keeps its state readable
